title: DevOps / platform engineer
summary: Linux, networking, Git, containers, pipelines and Kubernetes, with live labs on real machines: the platform other teams build on.
outcome: Ready to run and debug Linux hosts, build images and pipelines, and operate a Kubernetes deployment through a bad release.

stages.title: Linux and the shell
stages.why: Every server, container and CI runner is Linux. Files, permissions, processes, services and scripts are the ground floor of every incident you will be paged for.
stages.milestone: Can log in to a broken Linux server and find the full disk, the runaway process and the bad permission

stages.title: Git, properly
stages.why: Infrastructure is code, and platform teams review and revert more than anyone. History surgery, rescue and the power tools keep main deployable.
stages.milestone: Recovers lost commits, bisects a regression and keeps a clean history

stages.title: Networks you can debug
stages.why: "It's the network" is a hypothesis you have to prove. Subnets, routing, NAT, TCP, DNS, HTTP and TLS, then real packet captures in the live labs.
stages.milestone: Traces a failing request from DNS to TLS to the route and names the broken hop

stages.title: Containers
stages.why: Images are the unit of delivery. Layers, caching, volumes, networks and Compose, then the production practices that keep images small and safe.
stages.milestone: Builds a small, cached, non-root image and runs a multi-container stack with healthchecks

stages.title: CI/CD pipelines
stages.why: The pipeline is the platform team's product. Jobs, caches, test stages, release strategies and supply-chain security decide how fast and how safely everyone ships.
stages.milestone: Can ship a containerised service with CI: tests, image build, scan and a gated deploy

stages.title: Kubernetes
stages.why: Most platforms schedule workloads on Kubernetes. Deployments, Services, config, probes and rollouts, and the failure states (CrashLoopBackOff, no endpoints) you will debug.
stages.milestone: Operates a Kubernetes deployment: rolls out, spots the bad release and rolls it back

stages.title: Secure and operate
stages.why: Platforms hold the keys. Certificates, firewalls, SSH hardening, logs and broker operations, ending with an incident night on live machines.
stages.milestone: Handles an incident: reads the logs, fixes the certificate or firewall rule, and writes it up
